title: Adaptive frequency profiles and attention pathway selector for GPU-specific prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce median end-to-end latency (prefill + first decode token) and tail latency for mixed small/long sequence workloads by choosing optimal attention kernel paths and GPU frequency profiles at request time. Scope: H100, L40S, A10 instance classes; respect MIG partitioning configurations and cluster-level clock policies. Deliverables: runtime selector that picks between fused/streamed attention kernels, toggles SM clocks within allowed policies, and schedules prefill/decode to minimize KV-cache contention. Must integrate with routing/fallback logic for Dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Selector integrated in runtime call path and exercised by CI; 2) Median prefill+first-decode latency reduced by >=10% on H100 1-GPU full partition for target RLHF-like prompt mix; 3) 95th percentile latency improved or unchanged; 4) No correctness regressions (logprob deltas within 0.1%) across test prompts; 5) Feature gated via runtime flag and rolloutable via console A/B.
success_metrics: Median prefill+first-decode latency, p95 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, average GPU power draw during busy windows, A/B user-facing latency impact. Target: median -10%, p95 <= same, throughput +5% for batched small requests.
background_and_rationale: Recent incidents and perf audits (see links) showed that a single static kernel selection and global clock profile results in suboptimal latency for mixed workloads: long prefill sequences favor high-clock fused kernels on H100, while many small prompts benefit from lightweight streamed kernels and lower clocks to increase packing density. MIG partitions further constrain available SMs; naive clock boosts on shared hosts caused thermal throttling in experiments. A dynamic selector can apply heuristics and learned profiles to choose the best combo per-request and per-partition.
approach: 1) Build a lightweight policy engine called 'freq-path-selector' that takes (instance_type, mig_partition_size, sequence_length_histogram, batch_size, requested_slo_hint) and returns (attention_kernel_variant, target_clock_profile, prefill/decode scheduling hint). 2) Implement kernel adapter hooks in the runtime to switch between FUSED_ATTENTION, STREAMED_ATTENTION, and TILED_ATTENTION kernels with minimal code paths. 3) Integrate GPU clock control using existing clock-manager with safe guardrails (max_delta_per_min, thermal-backoff). 4) Add telemetry (per-request tags) to measure outcome and enable offline ML tuning of selector heuristics.
tradeoffs_and_constraints: - Clock changes are rate-limited and may be ineffective on noisy multi-tenant hosts; so selector must prefer kernel choice over clocks when change not permitted. - Fused kernels are memory-hungry; on MIG partitions they may increase OOM risk. - Complexity: adding runtime branching increases maintenance and testing surface. - Security: clock manager requires elevated privileges in Private deployments; feature must be disabled by default there unless admin opts in.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Wire selector API and return types; add flags. Week 2: Implement kernel adapter and unit tests. Week 3: Integrate clock-manager calls with guardrails; run lit perf tests. Week 4: Canary rollout to dedicated pool (non-prod) and collect telemetry; iterate. Week 5: Broader rollout + console toggle and doc updates.
risks: Thermal/backoff behavior could make clocks counterproductive; ML-driven selector may overfit to synthetic datasets. Rolling back clock changes must be fast. Need careful canary thresholds to avoid user impact.
test_plan: - Unit tests for kernel adapter switching. - Microbenchmarks: prefill-only, decode-only, mixed (prefix 4096 tokens then decode) across H100/L40S/A10. - Multi-tenant MIG tests with small and large partitions. - End-to-end A/B on a staging workload (mirror of customer X) with telemetry hooks. - Regression checks for logprobs and tokenization artifacts.

2025-02-14: Luca: PoC kernel-adapter implemented; microbench harness added for H100 and L40S. Early numbers: fused kernel + clock boost improved median prefill latency by 14% on single full-GPU H100 for long sequences (>=8192 tokens).
2025-02-18: Perf team: Observed 7% p95 regression in mixed small-request workload when forcing fused kernels — likely due to increased queuing; added streamed kernel path tests.

2025-02-21: Thermal tests: aggressive clock boosts pushed host into thermal-backoff after 20 minutes. Decided to add rate-limits and a thermal-safety knob. Added "no-clock" policy for shared Dedicated pools.

2025-02-25: Design review: PM and Security reviewed feature; Security flagged clock-manager privilege requirements for Private installs. Marked security_review_required = true and added opt-in requirement for on-prem.
2025-02-28: Integration: Selector integrated behind runtime feature flag. Canary rollout scheduled for 2025-03-04 to internal dedicated pool 'perf-canary-2'.

2025-03-02: Telemetry: initial canary runs show median latency -11% on H100 canary (long-prefill workload), median +3% on L40S for short-request mix. Action: tune decision boundary for L40S to prefer streamed kernels for small batches.
next_steps: 1) Tune heuristics for L40S within 48h after canary. 2) Add rollout gating in console dashboard. 3) Prepare rollback playbook (PR + runtime flag off). 4) Schedule on-prem security review with SOC.
